summary.intent: Advance cipher-box v1.1 milestone to completion by fixing GSD bookkeeping gaps (Phase 47/48), implementing and shipping the deferred share itemName lazy-backfill feature (PR #505), then investigating and fixing a staging bug where file decryption fails after moving a file into a subfolder.
summary.outcome: PR #505 shipped and merged (new PATCH /shares/:id/item-name endpoint, web wiring, e2e spec, CodeRabbit plaintext-zeroing fix). Root cause of decrypt-after-move identified (FileMetadata re-encryption missing from moveItem and restoreFromBin); both fixes implemented with regression tests on branch fix/decrypt-fail-after-move, pending PR.

repo: The GSD resume-incomplete-phase invariant false-positives when a phase shipped via PR has no SUMMARY.md files on disk — the gate checks artifact counts, not git history. Workaround: backfill summaries or use --no-resume.

backfillSentShareItemNames fires ONLY via the SDK getCoveringShares callback triggered on owner file upload (packages/sdk/src/client.ts:155) — there is no 'sent shares list' page or Share dialog path that triggers it.

FileMetadata IPNS records are AES-256-GCM encrypted with the parent folder's folderKey at upload time. Any operation that reparents a file without re-encrypting FileMetadata will cause Decryption failed on next preview/download.
moveItem in sdk/client.ts never re-encrypted FileMetadata for the destination folder (latent bug since feature was built). restoreFromBin has the identical omission.

Signed commits are required on all PRs. The 1Password SSH signer (op-ssh-sign) can silently produce no signature in sandboxed Bash (exit 0, no gpgsig header) and can also hard-wedge (exit 128 'failed to fill whole buffer') requiring an app restart.
pnpm api:generate must run after any API endpoint change — a pre-commit check-api-client.sh hook will block commits if the generated client is out of sync.
gh pr create triggers a bot chore(release) push to the branch immediately after PR creation; must fetch+rebase before any subsequent push.
web-e2e CI workflow has no push/pull_request trigger — it runs only on main-push (via workflow_call) or manual dispatch. New specs are not gated on PRs automatically.
CreateShareDto.itemNameEncrypted is @IsOptional (create-share.dto.ts:91), so a legacy NULL row IS creatable via direct API POST even though the web createShare() always sends ciphertext.

BinEntry stores originalParentIpnsName but not the encrypting folderKey. The current UI always restores to the original parent (source == target, no-op), which is why the restoreFromBin bug is latent rather than user-visible like moveItem.

code.finding: backfillSentShareItemNames was not zeroing the plaintext itemName Uint8Array after ECIES wrapping — sensitive bytes left in memory. CodeRabbit finding: wrap+persist in try/finally and fill(0) both plaintext and ciphertext buffers.

moveItem re-encrypt fix: guarded by if (movedItem.type === 'file'), resolves FileMetadata with source.folderKey, calls updateFileMetadata with dest.folderKey + createVersion:false. Runs inside withOperation before either folder publish so failure aborts the move atomically.
filePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted is string | undefined — tsc caught this but vitest (esbuild, no typecheck) missed it. Must guard before passing to hexToBytes.

restoreFromBin re-inserts FilePointer + publishes folder metadata but never calls resolveFileMetadata/updateFileMetadata to re-encrypt FileMetadata IPNS record. Identical class of bug as moveItem. Fix: resolve source folderKey from originalParentIpnsName via folderTree, re-encrypt only when target != originalParent.
getCoveringShares is called unconditionally on every addToFolder/reWrapNewItems, making any owner file upload a deterministic trigger for backfillSentShareItemNames — exploited by the e2e spec.

New 7-step two-party e2e spec: seeds legacy NULL-itemNameEncrypted share via direct API POST, triggers backfill via owner file upload, polls GET /shares/sent for null→ciphertext transition, asserts hex != plaintext and longer than plaintext (ECIES overhead), asserts recipient display unchanged. Passes locally (52s) and in CI (188/188).

workflow: Use git cat-file -p HEAD to verify a gpgsig header exists directly — git verify-commit may report 'No signature' even when the commit is signed, if allowedSignersFile is not configured locally.

The GSD progress --next flag mechanically routes by artifact counts and can produce destructive suggestions (re-execute a shipped phase). Always verify by cross-checking git log before acting on the resume-incomplete route.

For two-party UAT scenarios assumed to be human-only: fan out workflow investigators to probe the harness before labeling them non-automatable. In this case a 'human-only' UAT became a fully automated CI-passing spec.

Spinning up a 4-agent parallel simplify review (reuse/simplification/efficiency/altitude) quickly converged on 'no fixes needed' — the value was confirming the code was already idiomatic, not just skipping cleanup.

When committing signed commits in the background (run_in_background), a 200s timeout is still not safe if 1Password requires a Touch ID prompt — use foreground with dangerouslyDisableSandbox instead for signing operations.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged twice: first silently (exit 0 but no gpgsig header, masked by git verify-commit misreporting), then hard-wedged (exit 128 'failed to fill whole buffer') requiring a user-initiated app restart.
roadmap.analyze returned empty plan counts, forcing manual directory scanning for the resume-incomplete-phase invariant check.
git verify-commit reported 'No signature' for a commit that actually had a gpgsig header — misleading diagnostic that caused an unnecessary re-signing attempt.
gh pr create immediately triggers a bot chore(release) push, making the branch diverge before STATE.md could be updated and pushed — required an unplanned fetch+rebase cycle.
web-e2e CI doesn't run on PRs, so the new spec couldn't be validated in CI until a manual workflow_dispatch was issued separately.
Background task notifications for signed commits were ambiguous — the success message was from a git cat-file exit-0, not from the commit itself, masking the actual commit failure.
open_items: fix/decrypt-fail-after-move branch has moveItem + restoreFromBin fixes with passing unit tests but no PR yet — needs shipping.
Web-e2e regression tests for move-then-decrypt and delete-to-bin+restore-then-decrypt are not yet written (captured as tasks).
Desktop/FUSE e2e verification for move-then-decrypt not yet done.
Within-share move is an unbuilt feature gap — when implemented it must re-encrypt FileMetadata to destination subfolder folderKey (same pattern as moveItem/restoreFromBin).
/gsd-complete-milestone for v1.1 not yet run — STATE.md reads 'ready to complete' but the milestone close step was deferred.
.planning/intel/ directory is untracked and predates this session — not cleaned up.
A second CI web-e2e run was not dispatched against the final branch HEAD (dbd65ac59, CodeRabbit fix commit) — the passing run targeted the prior commit (81b1a92e1).

The BinEntry type carries no folderKey field — if the original parent folder is deleted before restore, the source folderKey cannot be resolved from folderTree. A future improvement would capture folderKeyEncrypted on BinEntry at deleteToBin time.
